sam: Hey @support - customer on prod chat is seeing partial output then silence. Root req id: req_prod_7f9a. Client receives first SSE event with 'data: {"delta":"Hello"}' then nothing. They wait ~20s, then socket closes. Logs show 502 on edge proxy but runtime logged 200. Copied bits below.

maya: can you grab the request id, curl repro, and a debug-bundle? Also which SDK/version & region?

sam: region: us-west1, SDK: js@1.4.2. req id req_prod_7f9a. Curl we used to repro (from customer):

sam: ```
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_prod_7f9a" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o","input":"hello"}' \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream"
```

sam: customer tcpdump shows FIN ~20s after first chunk. Proxy logs snippet: 

sam: ```
[edge] 2026-03-15T14:02:21Z GET /v1/chat/stream 502 req=req_prod_7f9a upstream=rt-12 host=api
[runtime] 2026-03-15T14:02:21Z 200 req=req_prod_7f9a model=gpt-4o tokens=12
```

ryan: if runtime returned 200 but edge logged 502 it's likely Fastly/edge timeout or http2->http1 conversion issue. Check `Transfer-Encoding` and `Connection` headers. Can you capture the edge trace id? Fastly should show a digest.

maya: Sam—please run `curl --http2 -N` variation to see if h2 vs h1 differs. Also generate debug bundle: `support-bot collect-debug --req req_prod_7f9a --include=tcpdump,proxy,rt-logs` and paste the bundle id.

sam: ran collection, bundle id dbg-20260315-773. Attached minimal repro curl for us to run:

sam: ```
curl -v -N --http2 -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: repro_local_22" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o","input":"stream test"}' \
  "https://staging.api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream"
```

eng-ops-bot: Received dbg-20260315-773. Kicking off automated collection. Please include client stacktrace if available.

maya: I'll run the repro in staging now. If it reproduces, we'll run packet captures on edge and runtime and check for `RST`/`FIN` from intermediate proxy. If not, we'll try websocket variant `websocat ws://...` to rule out SSE parsing.

sam: noted. customer asked whether this could be client buffering on iOS. They said a corporate proxy/middleware is in path. Could be proxy coalescing small chunks.

ryan: also check if `Content-Encoding: gzip` present; some proxies buffer until buffer full. Try disabling compression for streaming.

maya: thanks. I'll report back with repro results and attach stack traces. :white_check_mark:

sam: thanks team :pray:

support-bot: debug bundle dbg-20260315-773 is available at https://internal.debug/bundles/dbg-20260315-773
